title: Magnetic configurations and excitations in high-$T_{c}$ multilayer nickelates
authors: Jun Zhan, Xianxin Wu, Jiangping Hu
abstract: We investigate the magnetic ground states and transverse spin excitations of bilayer and trilayer nickelates within a multi-orbital itinerant framework. For the bilayer system, although Hartree-Fock calculations slightly favor a double-stripe order, the calculated excitation spectrum of the single-stripe state, characterized by an anisotropic low-energy cone at $Q_{\text{BL}}$ and isotropic high-energy excitations near $Γ$, exhibits good qualitative agreement with recent RIXS and neutron scattering experiments. We further identify mirror-even optical interlayer modes at $Q_{\text{BL}}$ whose energies match the mirror-odd modes at $Γ$. For the trilayer system, both mirror-odd and mirror-even spin-density-wave states can be stabilized near $Q_{\text{TL}}$, with the mirror-odd state lower in energy in the parameter regime studied. The mirror-odd state hosts an additional nearly gapless mode dominated by the middle layer, while the mirror-even state contains only one acoustic branch together with two gapped optical modes. Comparison with available RIXS data favors the mirror-odd spin-density-wave scenario. Our results show that magnetic excitations provide a sensitive probe of the magnetic order and support a common itinerant origin of magnetism in multilayer nickelates.
summary: This theoretical study uses an itinerant multi-orbital framework to map out the magnetic ground states in multilayer nickelates. By calculating spin excitation spectra for various SDW symmetries, the authors argue that these excitations serve as a sensitive probe distinguishing between competing magnetic orders. The results strongly support the mirror-odd SDW state and confirm the itinerant nature of magnetism in these high-$T_c$ materials.
main_problem: The study investigates the magnetic ground states and transverse spin excitations in high-temperature superconducting multilayer nickelates to understand the microscopic origin of magnetism.
main_result: The calculations favor the mirror-odd Spin Density Wave (SDW) state in trilayer systems, while for bilayers, the single-stripe state's excitation spectrum shows good qualitative agreement with experimental RIXS and neutron scattering data.
method: Theoretical analysis using a multi-orbital itinerant framework Hamiltonian solved via Hartree-Fock mean-field theory, followed by Random Phase Approximation (RPA) calculations for spin susceptibility.
model_or_system: The system models bilayer and trilayer nickelates in the Ruddlesden–Popper phase, described by an itinerant model incorporating onsite Hubbard interactions and Hund's coupling on Ni $e_g$ orbitals. The analysis compares different SDW symmetries (mirror-odd vs. mirror-even).
key_observables: Transverse spin excitation spectra ($	ext{Im}[\chi^{+-}]$), magnetic order types (single/double stripe, mirror-odd/even SDW), and optical interlayer modes.

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field decoupling (Hartree-Fock) and the Random Phase Approximation (RPA) for excitations, which may neglect certain correlation effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Fermi surfaces, real-space magnetic patterns for different SDW states, and momentum/energy spectra ($	ext{Im}[\chi^{+-}]$) comparing various magnetic orders.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the bilayer case (single vs. double stripe), then moves to the trilayer case by comparing mirror-odd and mirror-even SDW candidates, culminating in a comparison of excitation signatures against experimental data.
why_interesting: While focused on magnetism, the itinerant nature of the model and the use of orbital degrees of freedom place it within the broader context of strongly correlated electron physics relevant to unconventional superconductivity mechanisms.
